title: Detect Merge Markers
summary: A Claude Code hook that blocks an edit when Git conflict markers are still sitting in the file the agent just wrote or changed.
description: Agents sometimes resolve a merge conflict halfway and leave the angle-bracket lines behind. This PostToolUse hook opens the file that was just edited and looks for a line starting with seven less-than signs and another starting with seven greater-than signs.

When both are present it exits with code 2, which feeds the message back to the agent so it cleans the file before continuing. Files over 2 MB, missing files and files with no markers pass without a sound.
useWhen: Rebase or merge with an agent doing the conflict fixes
Catch a half-resolved file before it is committed
Keep a broken build out of a pull request
Review a branch that was recently merged

hook.command: node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>{let j={};try{j=JSON.parse(d)}catch(e){}const f=(j.tool_input||{}).file_path;const fs=require('fs');if(!f||!fs.existsSync(f)||fs.statSync(f).size>2000000)process.exit(0);const L=fs.readFileSync(f,'utf8').split(String.fromCharCode(10));const a=[],b=[];L.forEach((l,n)=>{if(/^<<<<<<< /.test(l))a.push(n+1);if(/^>>>>>>> /.test(l))b.push(n+1)});if(a.length&&b.length){console.error('Merge conflict markers remain in '+f+' (opening line '+a[0]+', closing line '+b[0]+'). Resolve the conflict and delete every marker line before moving on.');process.exit(2)}process.exit(0)})"

example.prompt: Resolve the conflict in src/config.ts and keep both new options.
example.result: If the agent leaves a line starting with <<<<<<< HEAD in the file, the hook reports the opening and closing line numbers and the agent removes the markers in its next step.

faq.question: Will it flag a Markdown heading underlined with equals signs?
faq.answer: No. It needs both an opening and a closing marker line, each followed by a space and a label, so a lone row of equals signs is ignored.

faq.question: Does it check files the agent only reads?
faq.answer: No. It runs after Edit and Write calls only, and it looks at the single path given in that call.

access: Reads the file the agent just edited
Exit code 2 sends a message to the agent; nothing is changed on disk
